task.title: Update header nav for better UX
task.description:
Make the "deleted tasks: hidden" button and Publishing button an actual UI toggle:
These controls shouldn't be a text button, but a nicely designed toggle switch. Text "Show/Hide Deleted" and "Publish/Push" followed by the toggle. So e.g. when Deleted tasks are being shown, the text reads "Hide Deleted", and when auto publishing is turned off that text reads "Publish".

It also doesn't belong in the same nav control as the Board and Statuses link. For one, when you're on the Statuses page, the button disappears, which moves the position of the Board link as well - bad UI experience with nav links not in consistent positions.
So: move "Board" and "Statuses" links to be left-aligned in the top nav, next to the "Workbook Board" header.
Keep the Deleted and Publishing toggles right-aligned.


## Shipped (2026-08-16, PR #107)

One PR through a one-round adversarial execution-verified review (APPROVE, record on the PR), all browser evidence from real Chrome over CDP with trusted input events.

Board and Statuses links now sit left-aligned next to the "Workbook board" heading, byte-identical positions on both routes (measured at 1440x900, 1280x800, 1024x768, 390x844). The three settings became real toggle switches, right-aligned: Show/Hide Deleted (still an anchor driving ?deleted=1 - cmd-click, bookmark, and Back all preserved - with role="switch" layered on, Space and Enter both verified activating in real Chrome without scrolling the page), Show/Hide Descriptions (converted for consistency; flagged as a judgment call in the PR), and Publish/Push for publishing (off = inline mode per the story's example; on = watcher-deferred). Each label's width is measured and pinned so no switch moves across any of the eight label-state combinations; "Updated <time>" stacked above the switches so the clock cannot walk them. New header_nav_test.go (9 tests); 11/11 review revert-checks caught.

Recorded non-blocking findings: with deferred configured and no watcher answering, the switch reads off and activating it silently ping-pongs the server mode while the knob never moves - pinned by test, byte-for-byte the old text button's behavior, candidate follow-up to surface watcher absence; the "Publish" off-state announces to assistive tech as "publishing off" though both modes publish (label pair as specified, one-word change if wanted); Chromium-only verification (anchor role="switch" is best-supported in Blink).
